cards.html: This track takes you from solving one linear equation to the algebra an MSc in economics expects on day one: functions, polynomials, quadratics, exponentials and logarithms, systems of equations, vectors and matrices. It assumes the Math Foundations track: negatives, fractions, powers, expanding brackets, solving and rearranging equations, and straight-line graphs.

TopicWhere economics uses it
FunctionsDemand, supply, cost, utility and production functions
Polynomials and quadraticsCost and profit curves, finding maximum profit
Exponentials and logsGrowth, interest, discounting, log-linear regressions, elasticities
Systems of equationsMarket equilibrium, several markets at once, macro models
Vectors and matricesEconometrics (regression is matrix algebra), input-output models, optimisation

The tree splits into two paths after Functions:

  • Left path (polynomials): polynomials, factoring, quadratic equations, parabolas, then exponentials and logs.
  • Right path (linear algebra): systems of equations, vectors, matrices, determinants and inverses, then solving systems with matrices.

You can follow one path to the end or alternate. The boss review needs both.

• Work every example on paper before reading the solution.
  • Do the practice questions with the answers covered.
  • Matrices are written in this track with square brackets over several lines, like this:
A = [ 2  1 ]
    [ 4  3 ]

That is a matrix with 2 rows and 2 columns: the first row is 2, 1 and the second row is 4, 3.

  • A calculator is fine for exponentials and logs; for everything else, try without.
